chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Umm al-Walad fulfills the expiation for Dhihar."

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: A concubine who bears her master a child
key_terms.الظَّهَارِ: Dhihar, a form of divorce by analogy in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Who fulfills the expiation for Dhihar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that an Umm al-Walad (a concubine who has borne her master a child) suffices for the expiation of Dhihar, distinguishing her status from a free woman in this specific legal context. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the social status of the person freed as part of the kaffarah, emphasizing the completion of the obligation through the emancipation of a slave regardless of her prior classification as a concubine.
